name: Breathing Room
core: Adversarial group-liberty capture and living territory.
stateActions: 7×7 intersections. Alternate placing stones or passing. Orthogonal groups with no empty neighboring liberty are removed after enemy captures resolve. Suicide prohibited; positional superko prevents repeat boards. Two consecutive passes enter explicit territory scoring with disputed groups played out, never guessed dead. Area = stones plus empty regions bordering only one side; compensation displayed before play.
decisions: Connect threatened groups or sacrifice them for outside influence; start a capture race, invade, or secure two independent eyes. Occupying an empty point can save one group while taking a liberty from another.
depth: Generated balanced opening studies plus full matches; opponent reads short liberty races and protects eyes. At least three ordinary victories must require saving a group, sacrificing stones, and playing a boundary dispute across separate starts.
winLoss: Higher area after agreed double pass wins, equality draws; opponent area win is a natural loss. Resignation optional but never failure evidence.
controls: Tap an intersection; preview liberty/capture consequences; Confirm placement. Arrow focus with Enter; separate Pass button.
accessibility: Every point names coordinates/owner/group/liberty count. Region score table and captured-stone log; no color-only ownership.
qa: Public practice capture: white C3 has B3/C2/C4 occupied by ink and D3 empty; place D3 and confirm removal before continuing a full match to scored victory.
Public life study: preserve two eyes against house pressure; independently play full match to win from shown rules, logging all moves.
Failure: invade a sealed region, permit capture, then finish double-pass scoring below house. Verify superko rejection does not consume turn.

name: Homeward Pips

stateActions: Two-player community-card poker with explicit simplified fixed-limit betting. Each starts40 chips, blinds1/2 alternate. Two private cards each; shared flop3, turn1, river1. Betting before flop/after each reveal, up to three raises per street, raise size2 preflop/flop and4 turn/river. Check if no owed bet, call matching owed, fold surrender pot, raise if affordable. Equal stacks; all-in caps contest to matched contribution, refund unmatched excess. Best five of seven using displayed standard rank table wins showdown; ties split. Eight hands or bankruptcy ends.
decisions: Continue a draw when price warrants or fold mediocre made hand, bet value versus bluff based on public texture/opponent history, avoid raising a dominated hand, manage match lead and finite bankroll.
depth: House samples plausible unseen holdings conditional on public history and its own cards, never player private hand; mixed aggression with reproducible seed. Include ordinary wins involving both fold and showdown, not all-in coin flip.
winLoss: More chips after eight hands wins; fewer loses; equal draws. Bankruptcy terminal loss/win. No real money.
controls: Check/Call/Fold/Raise buttons with exact resulting pot/contribution; optional hand-strength reference explains only visible player combination, not future odds oracle.
accessibility: Card ranks/suits text, betting history and owed amount, community versus private group labels; pending street clear.
qa: Win: fold a dominated-looking flop without losing rest of stack, later value-bet strong river and finish eight-hand profit.
Loss: call successive strong opposing bets with weak hand, lose bankroll via real showdown.
Verify cannot fold-check for free accidentally, raises capped, dealer blind alternation, split pots and unmatched all-in refund; AI unseen-card independence.

name: Rings Leave Ripples
core: Move a ring to leave a marker and flip crossed marker runs; scoring removes one of your own future movement bases.
stateActions: Hexagonal radius3 board,37 intersections. Alternate placing four own rings on empty cells, then movement phase. On turn choose own ring, leave own marker on its origin, move along a straight hex axis. May cross any empty intersections before markers; after first marker must cross entire contiguous marker run and stop at first empty intersection. Cannot cross another ring. All crossed markers flip owner; empty-to-empty move allowed. Any four collinear consecutive same-owner markers create scoring row. Resolve every row before next move: row owner selects four consecutive markers to remove, then removes one own ring permanently and gains one seal. If both sides have rows, mover resolves their own first; removing markers can break rival row. Multiple own rows resolve one at a time with choice. Victory immediately at third seal.
decisions: Choose ring origin that seeds a row while its landing enables a future crossing, flip an enemy threat without creating a stronger rival row elsewhere, choose which scoring markers/ring to remove to preserve future movement options. Scoring voluntarily reduces your mobile sources; greedy immediate row can leave a weaker remaining ring position.
depth: Four movable bases plus persistent two-color markers create positioning and forced-flip plans. At least three starts after placement; ordinary wins must involve deliberate marker reversal and non-nearest ring removal. Opponent searches ring moves plus scoring-removal choices. A repeat maximum-distance flip policy must fail across starts.
winLoss: First three seals wins; house three loses. If current player has no legal ring move before three seals, opponent wins. Threefold full-position repetition draws;100 completed ring moves without third seal draws with no score-based shortcut.
controls: Select ring then legal landing; preview crossed run and rows. During scoring select row endpoints then ring to remove; explicit confirm for each. Keyboard axial-coordinate cell list.
accessibility: Each intersection describes ring or marker owner and coordinate. Crossing-run list, qualifying row endpoints and remaining movement bases printed; owner patterns plus words; no timed resolution.
qa: Win: create marker row by crossing and flipping a mixed run, remove a strategically selected own ring, then maneuver remaining rings to earn third seal in full ordinary match. Repeat independent victory from different placement.
Loss: greedily flip a run that completes opponent row, allow their third seal and verify natural terminal loss; separately choose poor own ring retirement and continue to house victory.

Public referee study: simultaneous rows resolve mover first, selected marker removal can cancel other row; forced stop after contiguous marker run and inability to cross ring verified by rejected UI attempts.

Acceptance only with ordinary public fresh-start input transcripts and win/loss screenshots at exact source hash, no hidden model calls or solver route. Verify390px touch, keyboard focus, restart and slow readable scoring phase.

Independent full three-seal victories from two different initial placements are required; first scoring row is insufficient. Each transcript must explain selected ring retirement and show later movement consequences.
